notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); model-authored and unreviewed, with no hardware backend and no hardware run. The gate neither installed nor imported the clone, and the sim backend gymnasium.make("Quad-v0") was not run (upstream needs gymnasium, numpy, scipy, torch, matplotlib and vpython, setup.py:6-12, and its modules import args_parse). The fake backend is the package's own pure Python QuadEnv: it re-implements quad.py's nominal rigid-body dynamics with RK4 instead of solve_ivp/DOP853, uses random.Random(seed) while upstream's reset draws from numpy's global uniform and Python's global random (so its seed does not control the initial state), and does not model domain randomization, an actuator or contact model, rendering or the gymnasium wrappers; the fidelity gaps say this, and the model was never validated against a physical quadrotor. Expected warnings: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed only sets the seed of the next reset, so it makes no native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT for inputs the bridge derives (seed twice, ticks, and action.values[*]: the action values are normalized and dimensionless and the bridge derives the array, so no unit can be attached). There are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. Only catalogue classes cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1 and cap.world.seed.v1 are used, so there are no catalogue requests. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
